## Project Overview
The goal of this project was to design and build an autonomous rover capable of completing a course with five distinct tasks placed at random locations. The engineering team consisted of four members, collectively responsible for the mechanical design, electrical systems, and programming of the robot.

::: {style="text-align: left; margin-left: 20px;"}

![](old_scrappy.jpg){height="300px"}

*An early iteration of our rover*
:::


## Tasks
* **Leave Lander and Line Follow**
    The rover begins by exiting the lander and following a white line along the course. This was achieved using a QRD sensor array, which detects the rover’s position relative to the line and continuously adjusts its trajectory for accurate tracking.

    ![](QRD_array.jpg){height="300px"}

* **Sample Collection and Return**
    The rover detects the sample collection station using an IR sensor and positions itself to receive a ping pong ball. It then transports the sample and deposits it into the correct return bin based on color. This system combines IR and ultrasonic sensors for detection, along with a custom-designed ball capture and release mechanism.

    ![](sample_collect.jpg)
    ![](sample_return.jpg)

* **Canyon Navigation**
    In a section without guiding lines and enclosed by walls, the rover must autonomously navigate to the exit. This was accomplished using ultrasonic sensors to detect obstacles. When a wall is detected ahead, the rover turns in the direction with more open space, enabling efficient navigation through the canyon.

* **Data Transmission**
    After returning to the lander, the rover must locate an IR beacon and accurately aim a laser at a target. A servo-mounted sensor scans for the strongest IR signal, allowing the rover to align itself before activating the laser to hit the target reliably.

    ![](data_transmission.jpg)
